# Third-party notices

This file lists third-party software and data that Renderly distributes in its installers, with
the licence each one is provided under. It is **generated** by
`python scripts/third_party_notices.py` from the dependency graph and the package sources; do not
edit it by hand. Rust entries cover every target-specific dependency of the shipped crates, not
only the host target, so the list is a superset of what any single installer contains.

Renderly itself is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later (see
[LICENSE](LICENSE)).

## Bundled model, font and FFmpeg

### YuNet face detection model (face_detection_yunet_2026may.onnx)

- Licence: MIT
- Bundled in renderly-core via `include_bytes!` (`renderly-core/src/ml/models.rs`). Model origin: https://github.com/ShiqiYu/libfacedetection.train; distributed copy from opencv/opencv_zoo (see `renderly-core/assets/models/README.md`).
- Licence text: [T346](#licence-text-346)

### Roboto Bold font (Roboto-Bold.ttf)

- Licence: Apache-2.0
- Bundled in renderly-core via `include_bytes!` (`renderly-core/src/captions/mod.rs`), from `renderly-wasm/assets/Roboto-Bold.ttf`. Copyright notice, read from the font's name table (ID 0): Copyright 2015 Google Inc. All Rights Reserved. Licence description (ID 13): Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
- Licence text: [T347](#licence-text-347)

### FFmpeg

FFmpeg (`ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`) is bundled into the installers as separate programs. Its licence, source offer and build details are in [NOTICE-ffmpeg.md](NOTICE-ffmpeg.md).

### Robust Video Matting (downloaded, not distributed)

Robust Video Matting weights (used for background removal) are **not** distributed with Renderly. They are downloaded from the upstream host on first use, after the user consents, and pinned by SHA-256 (see `docs/ml-licence-review.md`). The model is licensed GPL-3.0 by its upstream; no copy of it is included in this file or the installers.

Test-only fixtures (for example OpenTimelineIO sample files) are not distributed and are not listed here.

````text
https://www.apple.com/legal/sla/docs/xcode.pdf

Or by typing `xcodebuild -license` in your terminal.

From reading the license, it is unclear whether distributing derived works
such as these crates are allowed?

But in any case, to practically use these crates, you will have to link, and
that only works when you have the correct Xcode SDK available to provide the
required `.tbd` files, which is why we choose to still use the normal SPDX
identifiers in the crates (Xcode is required to use the crates, and when using
Xcode you have already agreed to the Xcode license).
````
